answer: Randomized stake-weighted jury draw resists sybils: every answer is graded by a panel sampled unpredictably from the established-stake pool, so an attacker cannot foresee or pack a jury. Swaying a verdict requires owning a large fraction of total bonded reputation — an ocean of stake, not cheap clones. Splitting into many keys only spreads thin stake across a wide canyon of identities, each left on a narrow ledge the random draw almost never seats. Attacker cost scales with stake held, never with identity count.
